rubric_items.reason: All 25 acceptance criteria across S-1 to S-6 map to at least one TP. No criterion is untested and none is invented.
Every test is an API integration test. The plan explains why: the rules sit in a service over the database and the comparator is private. No e2e or manual tests are planned.
The window has boundary tests on both sides of 08:00 (TP-5, TP-6), a started-slot test and a local-midnight test. The new endpoint has 404, malformed-id 400 and Inactive 400 negatives.
Matches Vitest, Supertest, throwaway PostgreSQL, fixed clock and the api/test folder. It does not name the new file or the 'HMS-11 REQ-n:' title prefix that neighbouring tests use.
Titles are concrete and runnable, with fixed times, names and expected outcomes, e.g. 'dr. alpha before Dr. Beta'.

findings.text: Test naming is underspecified. Neighbouring tests start with 'HMS-n REQ-m:', but the plan has no TP-to-REQ mapping and no title prefix. It also does not name the new test file, so the strategy's requirement-ID naming cannot be checked.

cites.quote: Each test name starts with its requirement id (C2).
HMS-9 REQ-2 (T-7): days follow the hospital zone across UTC midnight
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID

findings.suggested_fix: Name the file (e.g. api/test/specializations-earliest-slots.test.ts) and give each TP its 'HMS-11 REQ-n:' prefix from the story trace.

findings.text: TP-17 expects 400 for a malformed id but says it covers S-4/AC3, which is about an unknown id returning 404. It is a useful extra negative test, but it does not prove AC3.

cites.quote: Negative: a malformed path id gives 400 before any lookup", covers: [S-4/AC3]
Given no specialization has the requested id, when staff call the endpoint, then it returns 404.

findings.suggested_fix: Trace TP-17 to the design's parseId behaviour (EP-1 / CO-1) or mark it as an extra input-validation negative test rather than coverage of S-4/AC3.
